basic_info.title: Finite Scalar Quantization: VQ-VAE Made Simple
basic_info.code_available: yes (official JAX/PyTorch snippets in paper + community ports)

method.input_representation: generic (images, depth, panoptic maps in paper; architecture-agnostic)
method.sequence_model: N/A (bottleneck design, not a sequence model)
method.training_signal: supervised/self-supervised reconstruction or downstream task loss (bottleneck-agnostic)
method.notes: Replaces a learned VQ codebook with a fixed per-dimension scalar quantizer: project to a small number of dims (e.g. 5-10), round each independently to one of a small fixed set of values (e.g. {-1,0,1}), giving an implicit codebook of size = product of per-dim levels, with straight-through gradients through the rounding op exactly as in standard STE-VQ. Because every dimension is quantized independently to values that already span its full range, there is no learned codebook to collapse -- no commitment loss, no EMA codebook update, no code-splitting/reset heuristics, no entropy penalty are needed; full codebook utilization is obtained 'by construction'. Matches VQ-VAE-level reconstruction/downstream quality at comparable effective vocabulary size with a much simpler training recipe. NOTE: this is a discretization-scheme paper, not a categorical-RSSM paper -- it targets VQ-style codebooks, not DreamerV3-style independent per-group softmax categoricals with a fixed free-bits floor. Relevant to our project only as an architectural alternative (replace the KL-regularized categorical groups with FSQ-style fixed scalar bins) if free-bits/unimix tuning is abandoned -- NOT a drop-in fix for the current recipe, since it removes the KL term (and therefore free bits / KL balancing / unimix) entirely rather than adjusting it.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Not a map-matching, RL, or world-model paper -- cited purely as a dead-code/collapse-avoidance precedent for categorical/discrete latent bottlenecks, one of three literature gaps (VQ-style dead-code revival) explicitly requested in a 2026-07-26 research task on WM latent under-utilization.
gap_analysis.novelty_vs_recombination: N/A (engineering-design precedent, not a novelty anchor for the four-pillar system)
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Useful as context for why our current failure mode (dead categorical GROUPS under a KL floor) differs structurally from classic VQ-VAE dead-CODE collapse: FSQ sidesteps codebook collapse by removing the learned-codebook + KL machinery altogether, which is a much larger architecture change than anything justified by the current kl_act evidence.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Not BMW-relevant; logged as the 'discretization redesign' end of the spectrum of options for the kl_act~1-active-group finding, to be weighed against cheaper in-place fixes (per-group free-bits floor lowering, adaptive/scheduled free bits, pseudo-label sharpening) before considering any bottleneck redesign.

uncertain: Not verified from a full read whether FSQ has been combined with DreamerV3-style RSSM dynamics/representation losses (KL balancing) in any published work as of 2026-07 -- searches did not surface such a combination; treat as an untested architectural direction, not a validated fix for RSSM collapse specifically.
